question:
At a birthday party, children are being served orange juice in conical cups, as shown in the figure. Each cup is 15 cm deep and has a radius 5 cm. The juice is being poured into this cup at a rate of $0\cdot1~cm^{3}/s$.

On the basis of the above information, answer the following questions :

**(i)** Establish a relation between the height h of the juice in the cup and radius r of the surface of the juice in the cup, if the semi-vertical angle of the cone is $\alpha$.
**(ii)** At what rate is the juice level in the cup rising when the juice is 6 cm deep?
**(iii) (a)** When the juice is 6 cm deep, then find at what rate is the upper surface area of juice increasing?
OR
**(iii) (b)** When the juice is 6 cm deep, then find the rate at which the wetted surface area of the cup is increasing.
explanation:
(i)

Step 1 From the geometric profile of a cone, the semi-vertical angle $\alpha$ relates the radius and height. For the full cup, $\tan\alpha = \frac{\text{Radius}}{\text{Height}} = \frac{5}{15} = \frac{1}{3}$. For the juice level, $\tan\alpha = \frac{r}{h}$. Equating these gives $\frac{r}{h} = \frac{1}{3} \implies r = \frac{h}{3}$.

(ii)

Step 1 The volume of liquid in a cone is $V = \frac{1}{3}\pi r^2 h$. Substituting $r = \frac{h}{3}$ allows us to express the volume solely in terms of height: $V = \frac{1}{3}\pi \left(\frac{h}{3}\right)^2 h = \frac{\pi h^3}{27}$.

Step 2 Differentiate the volume equation with respect to time $t$: $\frac{dV}{dt} = \frac{3\pi h^2}{27}\frac{dh}{dt} = \frac{\pi h^2}{9}\frac{dh}{dt}$. Given that $\frac{dV}{dt} = 0.1\text{ cm}^3/s$, substitute $h = 6\text{ cm}$ to solve for $\frac{dh}{dt}$: $0.1 = \frac{\pi (6)^2}{9}\frac{dh}{dt} \implies 0.1 = 4\pi \frac{dh}{dt} \implies \frac{dh}{dt} = \frac{1}{40\pi}\text{ cm/s}$.

(iii) (a)

Step 1 The upper surface area of the liquid is a circle: $A = \pi r^2 = \pi \left(\frac{h}{3}\right)^2 = \frac{\pi h^2}{9}$. Differentiating with respect to time $t$ gives $\frac{dA}{dt} = \frac{2\pi h}{9}\frac{dh}{dt}$.

Step 2 Substitute $h = 6\text{ cm}$ and $\frac{dh}{dt} = \frac{1}{40\pi}\text{ cm/s}$ into the equation: $\frac{dA}{dt} = \frac{2\pi(6)}{9} \cdot \frac{1}{40\pi} = \frac{12\pi}{360\pi} = \frac{1}{30}\text{ cm}^2/s$.

(iii) (b)

Step 1 The wetted surface area is the lateral area of the cone: $S = \pi r l = \pi r \sqrt{r^2+h^2}$. Substituting $r = \frac{h}{3}$ gives $S = \pi \left(\frac{h}{3}\right)\sqrt{\frac{h^2}{9}+h^2} = \frac{\sqrt{10}\pi h^2}{9}$. Differentiating with respect to time gives $\frac{dS}{dt} = \frac{2\sqrt{10}\pi h}{9}\frac{dh}{dt}$.

Step 2 Substitute $h = 6\text{ cm}$ and $\frac{dh}{dt} = \frac{1}{40\pi}\text{ cm/s}$ into the derivative equation: $\frac{dS}{dt} = \frac{2\sqrt{10}\pi(6)}{9} \cdot \frac{1}{40\pi} = \frac{\sqrt{10}}{30}\text{ cm}^2/s$.
